headline: Approved a certificate of compliance for 231 Lexington Street; continued the Eversource parking lot project at 206 Calvary Street.
summary: Eversource plans to repave the parking lot and add stormwater treatment. Commissioners asked about snow storage, road salt, and transformer storage. The commission also approved draft language for conservation restrictions.
decisions: Continued the Eversource parking lot project hearing to the 11/19 meeting, 6-0.
Approved issuing a Certificate of Compliance for 231 Lexington Street, 6-0.
Approved the conservation restriction certification language and sign-off, 6-0.
Approved the minutes of the 10-22-2026 meeting, with Ms. Limonciello abstaining.

decision_titles: Eversource parking lot project at 206 Calvary Street
Certificate of Compliance for 231 Lexington Street
plain_text:
Approved 11/19/2026 
  
 
Waltham Conservation Commission 
November 5, 2026 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Meeting took place via public Zoom call with participation information posted at City Hall, Government 
Center, and on the Commission’s page of the city web site. Zoom information was circulated directly 
to all applicants and others on the public agenda. 
Meeting called to order at 7:01 PM. 
Attendees: Chair Bill Doyle, Vice Chair Lisa Limonciello, Gerard Dufromont, Michael Donovan, Anja 
Shafer, Frank Fitzgerald. Conservation Agent Julia Abbott. 
Absent:  
 
Public Hearing 
Notice of Intent (DEP File # 316-tba) 
Applicant: Audrey Hunt / NSTAR Energy Co. d/b/a Eversource Energy 
Property Location: 180, 206-R12, 206 Calvary Street 
Project Description: Paving and striping of an existing parking lot, stormwater management 
infrastructure upgrades, and associated ancillary work. 
Present for applicant: Audrey Hunt and Lance Russell (Eversource), Jonathan Chidekel and Michael 
Howard (Epsilon), Cam St. Croix (SMMA). Mr. Chidekel presented. He noted that a DEP number has 
not yet been assigned. He noted a site visit earlier this week and questions from Ms. Abbott which will 
be addressed. He added that the team has realized that not all three parcels are owned by 
Eversource. The missing owner has signed the form and he has sent a corrected the WPA Form 3. 
He located the site for the commission, identified wetlands, then described existing conditions 
including several photos. The goal of the project is to improve efficiency and circulation by repaving 
and restriping, with general reorganization of the site. He highlighted areas to be repaved. Restriping 
will add a small number of parking spaces. New guardrails will be installed. Some storage areas will 
be reorganized. They will be adding stormwater management; the site currently has none. This will 
include a bioretention area to the northeast, a bioswale to the north, and a subsurface infiltration 
system to the northwest. Erosion controls will be installed before work. Temporary pads will be 
installed to prevent vehicles from tracking material offsite during work. They will also be seeking an 
EPA permit and will have an improved stormwater prevention plan. Demoed pavement will be 
removed. No stockpiling is expected. They don’t expect dewatering to be needed. He noted they will 
also make 12 borings to test and characterize the soil; locations were shown. These are exempt from 
the WPA. Snow storage will be in the northwest corner. This site is an emergency response center, 
so they need to function at peak. Curbing will also be installed. The site uses sodium chloride, and 
they expect to continue to do so. Ms. Abbott noted that this project meets the 10.58(5) 
[Redevelopment Within Previously Developed Riverfront Areas; Restoration and Mitigation] because 
the whole site is previously developed. There is also a small area of BLSF. She believes they meet all 
standards. They will provide more flood storage. She asked if the applicants have contacted
Approved 11/19/2026 
Waltham’s Engineering Department yet; they have not. She asked about the snow storage location. 
Ms. Hunt has talked to the on-site facilities staff and this location is the best option. This is a tight lot 
that needs to stay in operation and the only alternative is the northeast corner, which is heavily used 
during storm events. Ms. Abbott confirmed that DEP has not posted this application and has not yet 
made any comments. 
Mr. Donovan asked why snow storage could not be to the northeast. Mr. Howard explained their 
decision based on both logistics and proximity to the riverfront area, BVW, and flood zone. Mr. 
Donovan had concerns about the small size of the NW storage area. Discussion. Applicants stressed 
that this site is actively used and important during emergency response operations; if they allow snow 
to accumulate, it affects use of the site. If snow accumulation becomes an issue, they will need to 
remove it to maintain operations. Mr. Donovan asked into the time frame, and how operations would 
continue during work. Mr. Chidekel believes the project will take about two months. He did not have 
operational impact details. Mr. Donovan noted this could be a challenge. He asked for confirmation of 
stormwater capture and treatment details. Mr. St. Croix gave a detailed walk-through of the 
stormwater management. He began by noting that flow will be largely unchanged, but water will now 
be treated. He noted two new water quality units and infiltration in the northwest corner; a grass lined 
swale and bioswale along the north side; and a filtered bioretention area to the northeast. He stressed 
that there is no treatment at all today. Mr. Donovan prompted a discussion of the equipment storage 
area (for transformers). He also highlighted that the NW catch basin is under the snow removal area. 
Mr. St. Croix said they will look at adjustment options, as it is important that the drainage on the site 
be effective. Mr. Fitzgerald asked for confirmation that there will be no tree and large vegetation 
removals; there will not be, as there are none on the site. He asked for additional details on the 
transformer storage, regarding possible pollution risks. The applicants could not address all details, 
but Mr. St. Croix noted the bioretention area has been designed to capture any oil or other pollutants 
from the storage area. Ms. Limonciello asked for and received clarification on traffic flow and 
construction debris and materials stockpiling. Mr. Chidekel added that the entire site will be under a 
storm water pollution protection plan. Mr. Howard also noted that the results of the borings will 
determine if additional measures are needed (if there is contamination). Brief discussion of exemption 
status of test borings and potential additional measures if contamination is discovered. Discussion of 
salt/no-salt use in this area. Discussion of the applicant’s intent to continue to use NaCl at this 
location. Mr. Doyle noted that Waltham has no general prohibition; conditions are stricter in areas 
where water drains to the Cambridge water supply. Mr. St. Croix noted that the new water quality 
units are specifically designed to capture and mitigate this. Much will also go into infiltration and deep 
sumps. The bioswale and bioretention areas are also designed to capture and settle. These features 
will then be cleaned out semi-annually. Additional discussion of snow storage area placement (NE vs. 
NW). Ms. Hunt noted site use practicalities, while Mr. Howard pointed out that while both areas are in 
Riverfront, the NE area is also in Buffer Zone, so storing there would have greater negative impact 
(although both areas are already developed). Discussion of snow removal; the applicants stated 
again that the site is active during emergencies, and they would already need to remove stockpiled 
snow to maintain operations. Mr. Doyle commented that this is a redevelopment site, currently with no 
protections for the wetlands and river, so all this work will be an improvement. There was no 
comment from the public. Mr. Dufromont suggested the commission consider including snow removal 
as a condition. Mr. Doyle recommended the applicant work with commission staff to draft something 
acceptable, or include specific language in the O&M. The applicants agreed. Mr. Dufromont also 
commented on the continued use of salt, and the unanswered questions about transformer storage.   
Mr. Dufromont moved to continue to the 11/19 meeting. Seconded by Ms. Shafer. In favor: Doyle, 
Limonciello, Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Public Meeting 
Request for Certificate of Compliance (DEP File # 316-0607)
Approved 11/19/2026 
Applicant: Matt Tiano, Tiano and Tiano, LLC 
Property Location: 231Lexington Street 
Project Description: Expansion of an existing commercial building to include a 336 s.f. addition to be 
utilized as a loading area, a second story addition, and additional pavement for parking. Work also 
includes associated site development improvements to grading, landscaping and drainage. A later 
amendment to the filing increased the paved parking area by one space. 
Paul Finger of Paul Finger Associates was present for the applicant. He summarized the project and 
the work that was done. He noted a recent site visit with Ms. Abbott. The site is being sold. The 
current tenant stores a lot of material on the site, but they are moving and so will this material. Mr. 
Finger noted that ongoing and in-perpetuity conditions transfer to the new owner. Ms. Abbott reported 
on the site visit and has no concerns. She asked Mr. Finger to confirm that the proposed second-
story addition was not built; he confirmed that it was not. She recommended the commission issue a 
COC. Mr. Finger expressed concerns that any ongoing conditions be noted for the new owner; Ms. 
Abbott said she would explicitly note this on the COC form. 
Ms. Limonciello moved to issue, seconded by Ms. Shafer. In favor: Doyle, Limonciello, Donovan, 
Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
Mr. Daly from the commission office added that he had located the original OOC during the 
discussion and it appeared that no unusual conditions had been added, but the continuation of the 
standard conditions would be noted on the COC. 
 
Commission Business 
• Approval of meeting minutes from 10-22-2026. Ms. Shafer moved to approve, seconded by Mr. 
Fitzgerald. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Ms. Limonciello abstained. 
Motion passed. 
 
Correspondence 
• NOTED: National Grid plans  gas main replacement work in the right -of-way of Forest Street, 
fall/winter 2026-27. A portion is in buffer zone but is exempt maintenance activity. 
 
Old Business 
• Possible sch eduling of Paine/Storer boundary walk (Nov./Dec.).  Discussion. Scheduled for 
Saturday, 12/5, 10AM.  
• Conservation Restrictions. Update. Mr. Daly had no new information. As noted at the previous 
meeting, the request to the Law Department for a list of potential CR holders was redirected to 
the mayor’s office. The mayor responded that the CRs will be put out to bid. Discussion. Ms. 
Limonciello noted that it feels to her that the conditions in the drafts align with what t he 
Conservation Commission would issue. Due to this, she’s less concerned than  she had been. 
Mr. Doyle agreed. He brought up the “certification” language drafted by the office staff and asked 
if they had anything to add. Mr. Daly said he did not, and noted the draft language was based 
on the original language of the CPC applications for those parcels. He noted that the certification 
page is not strictly an endorsement of the CR, but a statement that the ConCom agrees  that a 
CR on the parcel is a good thing and notes the reasons. Mr. Doyle said that they should assume 
the CRs will be modified when holders are identified. Discussion of work previously done, 
jurisdictional issues. Noted that none of this removes ConCom/DEP oversight from parcels in 
jurisdiction (not all these parcels are in jurisdiction). Ms. Limonciello raised the issue of spec ific 
details flagged for closer review by Mr. Daly in a previous document. Mr. Daly felt that the 
commission had previously decided to set this part of the CR review aside and focus on  the 
certifications. He suggested that the commission could review  the certification language one 
more time, then decide if they were going to look at only the ones in jurisdiction or all of them,
Approved 11/19/2026 
then decide to vote on the language, either for each individually or as a slate. Ms. Shafer noted 
that it seems the ConCom is simply being asked to say that a CR is good and provides a lasting 
public benefit. The commission agreed. Mr. Doyle felt the commission could vote to approve 
them all at once, because there are no special conditions for any. Ms. Limonciello asked for 
confirmation that none of this would affect future jurisdiction, which Mr. Doyle agreed is correct. 
Ms. Shafer pointed out that the burden of challenging any proposed future changes to uses set 
under the CR would be on the CR holder. Mr. Daly also noted that any conditions on any of 
these parcels from past OOCs would not change. Mr. Doyle restated that the ConCom is just 
agreeing that this is a good idea; the nuts and bolts of these CRs are still far from being 
completed. He felt they might have a chance again, at that point, to offer opinions. Mr. Donovan 
asked about the signing procedure. Mr. Daly noted this wasn’t entirely clear; he was not certain 
that the commission’s adoption of electronic signatures (110G) applied in this case. Mr. Doyle 
suggested that it would be worth having everyone make the effort to sign. It was confirmed that 
no deadline has been presented for signing. Ms. Shafer made a motion that the commission 
approve the language and sign off. Seconded by Ms. Limonciello. In favor: Doyle, Limonciello, 
Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont.  Motion passed. Mr. Daly will prepare the forms for 
everyone to sign. Mr. Donovan asked if we know when the city plans to issue the RFP for these. 
That information hasn’t been shared with the commission.  
 
Site Visit Reports 
• 101 Elm Street (Prestige car wash). Ms. Abbott has spoken to the manager but has no additional 
information to update the commission and will follow up.  
• 44 Shore Road.  Construction debris. Ms. Abbott spoke to the contractor, who removed the 
dumped mulch. Gravel and sand are still there. She thinks there may have been a 
misunderstanding about the property lines and which material to move, and will follow up.  Mr. 
Dufromont asked about the property sale status. Ms. Abbott did not have information on this. 
 
Committee Reports 
• CPC: Next meeting scheduled for November 17. 
 
New Business 
•  
 
Motion to adjourn by Ms. Limonciello, seconded by Ms. Shafer. All present in favor. Motion passed. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:20 PM.
